title: Sell Mineral Rights in Devola, OH
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Devola, OH
metaDescription: Devola sits in Washington County near Marietta, where Utica flank and legacy oil production overlap. Learn what that means for your mineral interest.
heroLead: Devola sits just north of Marietta along the Muskingum River, in a county whose oil and gas history runs back to some of the earliest drilling in the state.
intro: Devola is an unincorporated community in Washington County, close enough to Marietta that many residents consider it part of the same area, and Washington County itself has one of the longest oil and gas production histories in Ohio, dating back well over a century before the Utica play was ever discussed. Positioned on the flank rather than the core of the modern Utica/Point Pleasant fairway, this part of the county has seen less horizontal drilling than counties like Noble or Monroe just to the east, but legacy production and mineral severances here run deep.

sections.heading: A county with two very different production eras
paragraphs: Washington County's oil history predates the shale era by generations, with shallow conventional wells scattered across the county going back to the 1800s. Modern Utica/Point Pleasant activity has been more concentrated in the eastern part of the county, closer to the Noble County line, which means a Devola-area tract's value depends heavily on whether it sits near any newer horizontal unit or only carries legacy conventional history.

sections.heading: What to check before assuming your minerals are inactive
paragraphs: Because Washington County has such a long production history, some old leases and mineral reservations here are easy to lose track of across generations. A search through the Washington County Recorder's index in Marietta will show any lease, assignment, or affidavit filed against your parcel, which is the starting point for figuring out whether your interest is currently leased, has expired, or was never leased at all.

faqs.question: Does Devola have any active Utica or Point Pleasant drilling nearby?
faqs.answer: Development in Washington County has leaned more toward the eastern townships near Noble County, so activity directly around Devola has generally been lighter, though that can shift as operators expand units.

faqs.question: What if my deed only mentions an old conventional lease from decades ago?
faqs.answer: Check whether that lease is still being held by production, meaning a well on it is still active, or whether it has expired under its own terms. The Washington County Recorder can confirm what's on file against your parcel.

faqs.question: How is my interest valued if there's no recent drilling nearby?
faqs.answer: Without recent activity, valuation leans on your net mineral acres and any historical production your tract has seen, priced conservatively relative to interests sitting inside actively producing units.

faqs.question: Is Washington County part of the Utica core or the flank overall?
faqs.answer: It's mixed. Western townships near Marietta, including the Devola area, have generally been on the flank, while eastern townships closer to Noble County have seen more core-style development.
